questions.question: Write a short note on Tuhafat-ul-Mujahiddin. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Tuhafat-ul-Mujahiddin is an Arabic historical work written in 1583 by Zainuddin
  • Makhdoom II of Ponnani. It records Portuguese atrocities in Malabar from 1498 to
  • 1583. The text highlights resistance by Mappila Muslims, Kunjali Marakkars and
  • the Zamorin of C alicut. It is the first authentic native source on 16th -century
  • Kerala and calls for jihad against the Portuguese.

questions.question: Explain the“Blood and Iron” policy of Marthanda Varma. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Marthanda Varma’s “Blood and Iron” policy meant the use of force and warfare to
  • centralise power in Travancore. He crushed the Ettuveetil Pillamar and internal
  • rivals. He modernised the army with European help under Capt. De Lannoy. The
  • policy established absolute monarchy and royal monopoly over trade.

questions.question: Write a short note on Third Anglo-Mysore War. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• The Third Anglo -Mysore War was fought from 1790 to 1792 between Tipu Sultan
  • and the British -led alliance. Tipu’s attack on Travancore and suppression of
  • Malabar rebellions triggered the war. The Treaty of Seringapatam in 1792 forced
  • Tipu to cede Malabar to the British. This strengthened British control over the
  • pepper trade in Kerala.

questions.question: Write a short note on sambandham marital relations in Kerala. / [CO1, CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Sambandham was a traditional non -sacramental marriage system followed by
  • Namboothiri and allied communities in matrilineal Kerala. The alliance was
  • temporary and the Nair woman stayed in her taravad. Children belonged to the
  • mother’s lineage and the husband had no property rights. The system declined
  • under colonial influence and reform movements.

questions.question: How did colonial law reinforce patriarchy in Kerala? / [CO1, CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Colonial law reinforced patriarchy by applying Victorian norms to matrilineal
  • customs. The Malabar Marriage Act of 1896 and Nair Regulation of 1925 ended
  • marumakkathayam. These laws promoted nuclear families and individual male
  • property rights. They weaken ed women’s position in the taravad and shifted
  • society towards patriliny and monogamy.

questions.solution_html:

  • blended community grievances with alternative histories such as ancient
  • Buddhist Kerala versus Brahminical domination. The petitions served as tools for
  • Ezhava mobilisation and rights demands. This style became an early form of
  • modern historiography in Kerala.

  • historical injustice. The petitions directly paved the way for the SNDP Yogam and
  • the anti-caste movement in Travancore.

questions.question: What is the significance of Payyannur Satyagraha? / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Payyannur Satyagraha was the 1930 Salt Satyagraha centre in Malabar led by K.
  • Kelappan. The march from Kozhikode to Payyannur broke the salt law at Uliyath
  • Kadavu. British forces raided the camp. It was called the Second Bardoli and
  • boosted the Civil Disobedience Movement across Kerala.

questions.solution_html:

  • Vimochana Samaram in Kerala. It operated mainly in Kuttanad and was backed by
  • church and landlord interests. The group attacked communists and supporters
  • opposing land refor ms. It symbolised organised resistance to the first elected
  • communist ministry.

  • Reorganisation Act of 1956. The merger created a single Malayalam -speaking
  • Kerala state on 1 November 1956. It achieved linguistic and administrative unity
  • for the entire Malayalam region.

questions.question: Analyse the factors that led to the Attingal Revolt against the English East India Company. / [CO1, CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• The Attingal Revolt of 1721 was the first major anti-British uprising in Kerala at the
  • Anjengo factory. Economic grievances included the Company’s pepper
  • monopoly, corrupt practices and forced labour. Local chiefs rose against political
  • interference and atrocities. The British suppressed the revolt but it forced them to
  • shift focus to Travancore.

  • ending feudal anarchy. He curbed the influence of powerful nobles including the
  • Paliath Achan. He centralised administration and planned the modern town of
  • Thrissur. He promoted the T hrissur Pooram festival to unite communities while
  • balancing British relations.

  • created export dependency. British agency houses and land -revenue changes
  • deepened inequalities. In frastructure such as roads and ports developed but
  • long-term economic dependence also grew.

questions.question: Analyse in detail the impact of colonialism on the Princely State of Travancore, with special reference to changes in administration, revenue system, social structure, and the overall process of state formation. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Colonialism profoundly impacted the Princely State of Travancore through
  • indirect rule after the 1795 subsidiary alliance. Administration was modernised
  • with a centralised bureaucracy and Dewan system. Revenue policy shifted to
  • cash-based land tax and roya l monopolies on cash crops. Social structure saw
  • missionary education and reform movements that both challenged and initially
  • reinforced inequalities. Overall state formation moved from feudalism to a
  • modern princely state that later faced demands for responsible government. The
  • process combined modernisation with economic exploitation.

  • Payyannur reflected the move to class -based politics. Together they show the
  • evolution of Congress strategy in Malabar.

questions.question: Critically evaluate the feasibility of the American Model in Travancore. / [CO4] [10x2 = 20]
questions.solution_html:
• The American Model proposed by C.P . Ramaswami Iyer in the 1940s aimed at an
  • American-style federal democracy for independent Travancore. It promised
  • modern administration and efficient governance. However it ignored local feudal
  • and caste realities and was seen as pro -British and anti -integration. The model
  • proved unrealistic amid strong mass movements for responsible government. It
  • was ultimately rejected and Travancore joined the Indian Union in 1949. The
  • proposal symbolised elite resistance rather than genuine democratic feasibility.
